subject: general
question: Sapna invested ₹20,300 on simple interest, partly at the rate of 5% per annum and partly at the rate of 9% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 7 years, then find the sum invested at the rate of 5% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Simple Interest** is equal for two investments, the ratio of **Principal** is inverse to the product of **Rate × Time**.

P₁ : P₂ = (1 / R₁T₁) : (1 / R₂T₂)

Since time (7 years) is the same, P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 9 : 5

Total units = 9 + 5 = 14 units → ₹20,300

Investment at 5% (9 units) = (20,300 ÷ 14) × 9 = 1,450 × 9 = ₹13,050

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,050.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total Principal = ₹20,300 | Time (T) = 7 years | Rate₁ (R₁) = 5% | Rate₂ (R₂) = 9%

**Formula:** Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a481ea38c41599122414e2bf46ff26d20bb84d5b5397d1e7131682c8d340d92.png] 

Let the amount invested at 5% be P₁ and at 9% be P₂.

⇒ (P₁ × 5 × 7) ÷ 100 = (P₂ × 9 × 7) ÷ 100

⇒ 35 × P₁ = 63 × P₂

⇒ 5 × P₁ = 9 × P₂ (Dividing by 7)

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = 9 / 5

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 9 + 5 = 14

⇒ 14 parts = ₹20,300

⇒ 1 part = 20,300 ÷ 14 = ₹1,450

⇒ Principal at 5% (P₁) = 9 × 1,450 = ₹13,050

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,050.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest on Multiple Parts

If a sum P is divided into n parts such that the simple interest on each part is equal, the ratio of the parts is P₁ : P₂ : ... : Pₙ = (1/R₁T₁) : (1/R₂T₂) : ... : (1/RₙTₙ).

Equal Amount Condition

If the total amount (Principal + Interest) is equal for all parts, then the ratio of investment is P₁ : P₂ = 1/(100 + R₁T₁) : 1/(100 + R₂T₂).

Principal vs Amount

Always identify if the question mentions **equal interest** or **equal amount** at maturity, as the ratio logic changes completely.
